claims.source: 341st Strategic Missile Wing History, 1 Jan - 31 Mar 1967, p 32, in the 341st Space Wing FOIA release of 14 June 2001, https://documents.theblackvault.com/documents/ufos/malmstromufo.pdf
claims.text: The wing history records that on 16 March 1967 at 0845 all sites in Echo Flight shut down with No-Go indication of Channels 9 and 12 on the Voice Reporting Signal Assemble, that all launch facilities in E Flight 'lost strategic alert nearly simultaneously', and that no other Wing I configuration lost alert at that time.

claims.source: 341st Strategic Missile Wing History, 1 Jan - 31 Mar 1967, p 38, https://documents.theblackvault.com/documents/ufos/malmstromufo.pdf
claims.text: The same history states at page 38: 'Rumors of Unidentified Flying Objects (UFO) around the area of Echo Flight during the time of fault were disproven', and records that a Mobile Strike Team questioned about the morning of 16 March 1967 'stated that no unusual activity or sightings were observed'.

claims.source: 341st Strategic Missile Wing History, 1 Jan - 31 Mar 1967, pp 38 and 40, https://documents.theblackvault.com/documents/ufos/malmstromufo.pdf
claims.text: The history records that the 801st Radar Squadron, Malmstrom AFB, 'gave a negative report on any radar or atmospheric interference problems related to Echo Flight', and that a comparable multi-facility shutdown had occurred at Alpha Flight on 19 December 1966 with the same capsule crew, adverse weather and a commercial power failure.

claims.source: 341st Space Wing FOIA release of 14 June 2001, full text, https://documents.theblackvault.com/documents/ufos/malmstromufo.pdf
claims.text: No launch control officer is named anywhere in the eighty-seven page release: the only officer named in the Echo Flight section is 'Capt. Bradshaw in the command post', and the names Figel, Salas and Carlson do not appear.

desc: Excerpts from five quarterly histories of the 341st Strategic Missile Wing, Malmstrom AFB, released to John Greenewald Jr by Headquarters 341st Space Wing on 14 June 2001 and posted by The Black Vault. The January to March 1967 volume carries a section headed 'the investigation of Echo Flight incident and the results' at pages 32 to 40, footnoted throughout to a single classified engineering report of 23 March 1967. The release is the document the board's Malmstrom node names as decisive. It states the shutdown happened and states that the UFO reports around it were disproven, and it names no launch officer on duty.
